podcast.title: Breakthrough at 37 (1998)
podcast.body: Dan Wilson achieved significant success at age 37, in early 1998, with Semisonic's hit song "Closing Time," after many years of trying to make it in the music industry. "When that song came out in early 1998, it quickly became a monster. And after years of trying to make it, it finally happened to Dan Wilson. He was 37."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Collaborated with Weezer
podcast.body: Dan Wilson from Semi-Sonic was among the outside collaborators brought in for Weezer's album "Ratitude." "Dan Wilson from Semi-Sonic."

podcast.title: Early Career as Artist and Environmentalist
podcast.body: Before his musical breakthrough, Dan Wilson worked as an artist and environmentalist, with music being a side interest. "He began working as an artist and an environmentalist, dabbling in music on the side."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Successful Songwriting Career
podcast.body: After his success with Semisonic, Dan Wilson has had a highly lucrative career as a songwriter, earning "real money." He penned at least six songs for The Dixie Chicks (including a Grammy winner for Song of the Year), three songs for Adele's *21* album (including "Someone Like You"), and co-written with numerous other major artists such as Taylor Swift, Tom Morello, Celine Dion, John Legend, and Pink. "But it is as a songwriter where Dan has made the real money."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Dan Wilson's Songwriting Prowess
xref.body: Guitarist and singer Dan Wilson has achieved considerable recognition as a highly sought-after professional songwriter. He co-wrote Adele's massive global hit "Someone Like You," which topped charts in dozens of countries and earned him a Grammy for Song of the Year. He also received a Grammy for his production work on Adele's "21" album and was nominated for a Grammy for writing "Not Ready to Make Nice" for the Dixie Chicks. His extensive songwriting credits include collaborations with dozens of other notable acts, such as Fantagram, John Legend, Steve Perry, Josh Groban, Jason Barraiz, Leanne Rhyme, Stevie Nick's Halsey Cold War Kids, K-Flay, Weezer, Panic at the Disco, and Taylor Swift. "But the big story here is guitarist and singer Dan Wilson. He's become a renowned songwriter for hire."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: External Collaborators and Multiple Producers for Ratitude
xref.body: For "Ratitude," Weezer brought in outside collaborators for the first time, including Jermaine Dupri, members of All-American Rejects, Lil Wayne, Dan Wilson from Semi-Sonic, and the guys from Sloan (though uncredited and parts recorded in 2003). The album also had four producers, including Dr. Luke and Jacknife Lee, plus Rivers Cuomo, totaling five. "For the first time outside collaborators were brought in, including Germain Dupree, a couple of guys from all American rejects, Lil Wayne, Dan Wilson from Semi-Sonic, and the guys from Sloan."
